did: An advisory session in the Nov 11 coordinator run, on server #764: the deny advisories job had been red on every PR for RUSTSEC-2026-0459, a flaw in the SQLite that sqlx 0.8.6 bundles. Measured first: the build compiles in sqlx's bundled SQLite 3.46.0, so every image carries it, whatever SQLite the image installs. No sqlx release reaches the fixed libsqlite3-sys 0.39: every 0.8.x pins ^0.30.1, and 0.9.0 stops below 0.38. So the session added a dated, reasoned ignore to deny.toml, after checking that every SQLite file the code opens is one this deployment wrote, including the read-only reopen of migrate's own VACUUM INTO backup. It wrote that down as an invariant in docs/storage.md, 'Which SQLite files are opened', which the ignore rests on. PR #784 went green with no Codex findings, the coordinator merged it as fdbfa96, and that closed #764.

calls.title: How to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0459
options: A dated, reasoned ignore in deny.toml, backed by a written invariant
calls.why: No sqlx release reaches libsqlite3-sys 0.39; 0.9.0 caps below 0.38. The flaw needs a database and -wal pair a less-trusted party wrote, and nothing here opens one.
calls.undo: Drop the RUSTSEC-2026-0459 entry from deny.toml once a sqlx-sqlite release accepts libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39, then bump sqlx.

calls.title: Where the invariant the ignore rests on lives
calls.why: It constrains which SQLite files are opened, not how much of home a service takes, and a comment in deny.toml is not where someone adding an import would look.
calls.undo: Move the section; deny.toml's comment points at it by name.

left: The ignore has a revisit date of 2027-02-11. Watch for a sqlx-sqlite release that accepts libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39, then bump sqlx and drop the entry.
Any future path that opens a database someone else supplied (an import, an uploaded backup) breaks docs/storage.md's invariant and must remove the ignore first.
cargo deny also warns that yoke-derive 0.8.3 is yanked. It is a warning only, and cargo update -p yoke-derive clears it. No issue was filed.
The calls above aren't in some-ui's docs/calls.json. The coordinator was offered C89-C92 for them.
